correctness.rationale: The block automorphism decomposition holds in every finite-field characteristic because the bracket is the universal alternating square. In dimension three exterior duality converts the fixed space of the derived action into the determinant-eigenspace dimension. The two-eigenvalue incidence formulas correctly count disjoint subspaces, graph lifts, upper-right blocks and fixed determinant fibers; Gaussian-binomial inversion recovers every joint coefficient. For d=-1 in odd characteristic the full-dimension term contributes the unique parity correction. Direct exhaustive finite-field enumeration at q=2,3,4 checks every bivariate coefficient and the separately built exterior-square matrices. The proof, not those finite checks, covers arbitrary prime powers.

originality.rationale: The full finite-field joint fixed-space distribution for the rank-three free class-two Lie algebra and its parity-sensitive fixed-point-free count were not covered by inspected primary material. Benito–Roldán-López describes an automorphism group decomposition over characteristic zero without enumerating graded fixed spaces; Burde–Dekimpe treats characteristic-zero existence and structure without finite-field counts. The nearest published-finding corpus Heisenberg result counts automorphisms of a three-dimensional, two-generator algebra, not the six-dimensional three-generator algebra, and it does not imply the present determinant-eigenvalue incidence distribution. Relevant general linear group inclusion-exclusion is acknowledged as a classical ingredient; novelty is not asserted for that ingredient alone.

A broader representation-theoretic classification of joint fixed-space distributions for A and its exterior square could imply this rank-three case under different terminology.
Searches and inspected sources cannot establish exhaustive publication priority.

value.rationale: The natural characteristic filtration of the first non-Heisenberg free class-two Lie algebra has two nontrivial three-dimensional automorphism modules. Their complete joint fixed-space statistics quantify both how often whole automorphisms are fixed-point-free and how the two graded obstructions interact. The exact positive binary-field count and the odd/even determinant correction are nontrivial structural features. This is a complete all-fields law, not a renamed generic GL(3) matrix rank count or an unmotivated isolated coefficient.
